detail.introHeading: A-level Maths tutoring from a teacher of nearly 40 years
intro: A-level Maths builds on itself. A gap in algebra from Year 12 shows up again in calculus, in mechanics and in statistics, and it costs marks on every paper. Tania finds where the understanding stops, explains the principle underneath, and then practises it on exam questions from your own board until it is secure.

Tania: Tania has taught A-level Maths and Further Maths for nearly 40 years, and still teaches at a top sixth form college, where she is very popular with her students.

She has a deep understanding of how students take in mathematics and of the best ways to help them learn. Parents and students most often mention how clearly she explains the reasoning behind each step.

detail.focusHeading: Where marks are won and lost in A-level Maths

focus.p: Algebra and functions is the most heavily examined area of the Edexcel specification, with more marks since 2018 than trigonometry, differentiation or integration. Slips in algebra are also how marks are lost in every other topic, so it is usually the first thing to secure.

These ask for the reasoning to be written out, not just a correct answer. Examiners report that students often cannot set up a proof by contradiction in the right language, leaving out words such as “assume”. It is a skill that improves quickly with practice.

focus.h: Statistics and the large data set
focus.p: Statistics questions expect a conclusion written in the context of the question, and both boards expect students to know their large data set. Hypothesis tests follow the same steps every time, and marks are lost when one of those steps is missing.

Kinematics and forces carry a large share of the applied marks. Most errors come before any calculation: a missing force on the diagram, or a sign going the wrong way. Tania teaches students to set a problem up carefully so the working follows.

faqs.q: Do you also tutor A-level Further Maths?
faqs.a: Yes. A-level Further Maths is taught by Emma, who has her own page on this site. Tania teaches A-level Maths.

faqs.q: When is the best time to start Maths tutoring?
faqs.a: Students start at every point in the course. Because each topic builds on the last, it helps to deal with a gap soon after it appears, often after a Year 12 test or mock, before the Year 13 content is built on top of it.

detail.introHeading: A-level Chemistry tutoring built around the exam
intro: A-level Chemistry is really three subjects: physical, inorganic and organic. Most students are stronger in one than the others, and the exam papers mix all three. Lessons start by finding which topics and question types are costing marks, then work through them using questions from your own exam board’s past papers.

Laraib: Laraib is a practising medical doctor who has tutored A-level Chemistry for eight years, with more than a thousand hours of online lessons. She achieved 11 A*s at GCSE and A*AAA at A level, and has over 60 five-star reviews from students and parents.

She explains each topic until it is properly understood before moving on. She sets homework after every lesson, uses regular assessments to show what is secure and what needs more work, and gives parents progress updates whenever they ask.

detail.focusHeading: Where marks are won and lost in A-level Chemistry

focus.p: Amount of substance is the most-examined topic on all three boards: 291 question parts on OCR A, 358 on AQA and 361 on Edexcel since 2016. At least 20% of the marks in A-level Chemistry need maths. Laraib teaches students to set out every step, so the method marks are safe even when the final answer slips.

A curly arrow has to start and finish in exactly the right place to score. Students practise each mechanism on their specification until they can draw it the way the mark scheme expects, then move on to synthesis routes that join several reactions together.

Every board sets extended questions that are marked by levels, not point by point. On OCR A there are two on every A-level paper. Students learn to answer every strand of the question in a logical order, which is the difference between a middle-level and a top-level answer.

Practical work is examined in the written papers: OCR’s practical activity groups, AQA’s required practicals and Edexcel’s core practicals. Questions on method, sources of error and improving an experiment come up every series, and they can be prepared for.

includes: One-to-one lessons for Year 12 (AS) and Year 13 (A level), usually one or two a week at a regular time

faqs.a: OCR A (H432), AQA (7405) and Pearson Edexcel (9CH0), at AS and A level. Laraib teaches other boards too: tell us which one when you get in touch.

faqs.q: When is the best time to start Chemistry tutoring?
faqs.a: Students start at every point in the course. Many begin after Year 12 mocks or in the autumn of Year 13. Starting earlier leaves time to secure the Year 12 foundations, such as moles, bonding and organic basics, that the Year 13 topics depend on.

faqs.q: My child needs a high Chemistry grade for Medicine. Can you help?
faqs.a: Yes. Most UK medical schools ask for A-level Chemistry at a high grade. Laraib is a practising doctor who achieved A*AAA at A level herself, and she sets harder questions and extension material for students aiming at A and A*.

detail.introHeading: A-level Psychology tutoring from a former AQA examiner
intro: A-level Psychology rewards three different skills: knowing the content, applying it to an unfamiliar scenario, and evaluating it. Students who revise the content alone often find their marks stall. Andy has examined for AQA, and each lesson covers a topic in full and then puts it to work on exam questions, which he marks and goes over.

Andy: Andy has taught A-level Psychology for nearly 30 years in top sixth form colleges. AQA is his specialism and he has been an AQA examiner, though he can teach every exam board.
He has a reputation for lessons that get to the point: the knowledge a question needs, the evaluation that reaches the top band, and how to use the scenario in application questions.

detail.focusHeading: Where marks are won and lost in A-level Psychology

focus.p: Research methods is the most-examined area of the course: 445 of the 1,208 AQA question parts in our question bank since 2016. It includes the maths, from choosing a statistical test to interpreting significance, and it is where many students drop marks they could keep.

A 16-mark essay is about 20 minutes of writing, and the top level needs evaluation that is developed, not just listed. Evaluation that only describes stays in the lower levels. Andy marks essays the way an examiner does and shows what would lift each one.

Many questions give a short scenario and ask students to apply what they know to it. Marks are lost when the answer is correct psychology but never mentions the scenario. Lessons practise using the details in the question, line by line.

AQA updated the Psychology specification for first A-level exams in June 2027. The papers and question types are the same, but some content has been removed or reworded. Andy teaches to the current specification, so revision time is not spent on material that has gone.

includes: One-to-one lessons for Year 12 and Year 13

faqs.a: Yes, if they sit A-level exams from June 2027 onwards, which includes students now in Year 12 and Year 13. The paper structure and question types have not changed, but some content has been removed or reworded. Andy teaches to the current specification.

faqs.a: Yes. Research methods and data handling come up on every paper, and the maths is the same few skills each time: choosing a statistical test, the sign test, significance and interpreting data. They can be learned and practised.

detail.introHeading: A-level Sociology tutoring from a former AQA examiner
intro: In A-level Sociology, most students know the studies and the theories. What separates the grades is how that knowledge is used: applying the Item, building an argument and reaching a judgement. Mark has marked these papers for AQA, and his lessons are built around what the mark schemes reward.

Mark: Mark has taught A-level Sociology for over 25 years and leads a very large and successful department. He has been an examiner for AQA, the board he knows best, and can teach every A-level Sociology specification.
He marks essays against the AQA levels and gives written feedback, so students can see exactly what would move an answer into the next band.

detail.focusHeading: Where marks are won and lost in A-level Sociology

focus.p: The 10-mark “applying material from the Item” questions and most of the essays come with an Item. The top bands need the Item’s points picked up and developed alongside the student’s own knowledge. Ignoring it, or copying it out, keeps an answer in the middle.

Papers 1 and 3 each end in a 30-mark essay, about 45 minutes of writing. Listing studies is not enough: the top level asks for analysis and for evaluation that reaches a judgement. Mark teaches a structure students can rely on under time pressure.

This 20-mark question has appeared on every Paper 1 since 2017. It asks students to apply a research method to a particular issue in education. Answers that describe the method in general, without tying it to the issue, are held in the middle bands.

Theory and Methods is examined on both Paper 1 and Paper 3, so it carries more marks than any single topic. Lessons link the theories to the topics students already know, which makes them easier to remember and to use in essays.

Essays marked against the AQA levels, with written feedback
